items.title: Mount the root filesystem read-only
items.rationale: Writable root filesystems make persistence and tampering easier after compromise.
actions: Move writable paths to explicit emptyDir or persistent volumes.
Validate startup scripts and temp directories still work after the change.
items.snippet:
apiVersion: apps/v1
kind: Deployment
metadata:
  name: REPLACE_ME
spec:
  template:
    metadata:
      labels:
        app: cua
    spec:
      automountServiceAccountToken: false
      containers:
      - name: REPLACE_ME
        securityContext:
          runAsNonRoot: true
          runAsUser: 10001
          runAsGroup: 10001
          allowPrivilegeEscalation: false
          readOnlyRootFilesystem: true
          capabilities:
            drop: ["ALL"]
          seccompProfile:
            type: RuntimeDefault

items.title: Reduce service account token exposure
items.rationale: Mounted service account tokens expand blast radius when a pod is compromised and should be disabled unless the workload truly needs Kubernetes API access.
actions: Set automountServiceAccountToken: false for workloads that do not need the API.
Use a dedicated least-privilege service account when API access is required.
Keep token mounts read-only and review RBAC bindings.
items.snippet:
apiVersion: v1
kind: ServiceAccount
metadata:
  name: sandbox-sa
  namespace: default
automountServiceAccountToken: false

items.title: Remove setuid/setgid binaries from the image
items.rationale: Setuid and setgid binaries create extra privilege-escalation paths even when the container is otherwise hardened.
actions: Remove unnecessary setuid/setgid binaries from the image.
Prefer distroless or minimal base images where possible.
Verify no operational tooling depends on privilege-granting helpers.
items.snippet: Rebuild the image without unnecessary setuid/setgid helpers.

templates.network_policy:
apiVersion: networking.k8s.io/v1
kind: NetworkPolicy
metadata:
  name: sandbox-default-deny
  namespace: default
spec:
  podSelector:
    matchLabels:
      app: cua
  policyTypes:
  - Ingress
  - Egress
  ingress: []
  egress:
  - to:
    - namespaceSelector: {}
      podSelector:
        matchLabels:
          k8s-app: kube-dns
    ports:
    - protocol: UDP
      port: 53
    - protocol: TCP
      port: 53
templates.service_account:
apiVersion: v1
kind: ServiceAccount
metadata:
  name: sandbox-sa
  namespace: default
automountServiceAccountToken: false
templates.kyverno_policy:
apiVersion: kyverno.io/v1
kind: ClusterPolicy
metadata:
  name: sandbox-restricted
spec:
  validationFailureAction: Audit
  rules:
  - name: require-restricted-security-context
    match:
      resources:
        kinds:
        - Pod
    validate:
      message: Enforce restricted securityContext for sandbox workloads.
      pattern:
        spec:
          containers:
          - securityContext:
              allowPrivilegeEscalation: false
              readOnlyRootFilesystem: true
              seccompProfile:
                type: RuntimeDefault
templates.gatekeeper_template:
apiVersion: templates.gatekeeper.sh/v1beta1
kind: ConstraintTemplate
metadata:
  name: k8srequiredsandboxsecurity
spec:
  crd:
    spec:
      names:
        kind: K8sRequiredSandboxSecurity
  targets:
  - target: admission.k8s.gatekeeper.sh
    rego: |
      package k8srequiredsandboxsecurity
      violation[{"msg": msg}] {
        input.review.kind.kind == "Pod"
        not input.review.object.spec.containers[_].securityContext.readOnlyRootFilesystem
        msg := "Sandbox pods must set readOnlyRootFilesystem=true"
      }

ai_advisor.executive_summary: Three issues raise a high-risk posture: service account token exposure and writable rootfs (both high), plus setuid/setgid binaries (medium). Remediations require workload or image changes and cannot be auto-applied safely.
ai_advisor.remediation_overview: Perform manual changes to the workload and container image: remove or restrict service account token usage, enable read-only root filesystem after ensuring writable paths are handled, and rebuild images without setuid/setgid binaries. Validate each change in a staging environment before production rollout.

prioritized_groups.title: Privilege and credential exposure
prioritized_groups.rationale: Service account tokens grant API access; highest impact and probability.

prioritized_groups.title: Filesystem integrity
prioritized_groups.rationale: Writable root increases persistence and tampering risk; requires app validation.

prioritized_groups.title: Image hardening
prioritized_groups.rationale: Setuid/setgid binaries enable privilege escalation; lower blast radius but should be removed in image rebuild.

item_advice.explanation: Pod has a projected or mounted service account token that could allow cluster API access if compromised.
item_advice.operator_impact: Requires workload changes: adopt least-privilege RBAC, use workload-specific service accounts, or implement Workload Identity/OIDC where available. Some app functionality may need API calls and must be adapted.
item_advice.validation_advice: Deploy to staging with new service account or token policies; run integration tests requiring API access and verify logs for denied calls. Confirm no required functionality breaks.
item_advice.ordering_reason: High impact if abused; fix before other privileges to reduce attack surface.

item_advice.explanation: Container root filesystem is writable, enabling file tampering or persistence after compromise.
item_advice.operator_impact: May require image changes or application adjustments (move writable paths to explicit writable volumes like emptyDir). Enabling readOnlyRootFilesystem can break apps that write to root-owned paths.
item_advice.validation_advice: In staging, mount root read-only and run full app workflows; ensure /tmp, /var/tmp, and declared workspace/artifacts volumes are writable and used by the app.
item_advice.ordering_reason: High-risk for persistence—coordinate with filesystem fixes and service-account hardening.

item_advice.explanation: Image contains setuid/setgid binaries which can be abused for privilege escalation.
item_advice.operator_impact: Requires rebuilding the image and removing or replacing these binaries; may require alternative tooling or capabilities.
item_advice.validation_advice: Scan rebuilt image to confirm removal, run runtime tests to ensure functionality is preserved, and verify no required tool was removed inadvertently.
item_advice.ordering_reason: Lower blast radius than tokens/rootfs but remove before production deployment to harden image.

ai_advisor.guided_operator_message: Prioritize removing service-account token exposure and enabling read-only rootfs in staging; rebuild images to remove setuid/setgid binaries. Validate each change before rolling to production.
warnings: Changes require application or image modifications—do not patch pods in place.
Enabling read-only root may break apps that write to root paths; verify writable mounts first.
Removing service account tokens can disrupt legitimate API calls if not accounted for.
next_steps: Create a staging deployment to test service-account and filesystem changes.
Identify and update code paths that call the Kubernetes API or write to root.
Rebuild container images removing setuid/setgid binaries and push to registry.
Run integration and security tests before promoting changes to production.
